headline_marked: Anthropic launches Claude Sonnet 5 [[for cheaper agentic AI]]
headline: Anthropic launches Claude Sonnet 5 for cheaper agentic AI
summary: Anthropic's new Sonnet 5 model offers agentic capabilities previously seen only in larger, more expensive AI models, now at a significantly reduced cost.
details: Anthropic has released Claude Sonnet 5, an upgraded version of its midsize AI model designed for enhanced agentic capabilities. This new model can plan, utilize tools like browsers and terminals, and operate autonomously, tasks that previously required more powerful and costly AI systems.

The release signifies a shift in the AI landscape, where agentic functionality is becoming a standard offering across different price points. The key differentiator for companies now lies in the affordability and reliability of these agentic AI services, rather than just their existence.

Sonnet 5 is engineered to deliver performance comparable to Anthropic's top-tier Opus 4.8 model but at a substantially lower price. It will serve as the default model for free and Pro plan users, with introductory pricing at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens until August 31, after which it will increase to $3 and $10 respectively.

Compared to its predecessor, Sonnet 4.6, the new Sonnet 5 demonstrates marked improvements in agentic tasks such as reasoning, coding, and knowledge work. For instance, it achieved a 63.2% score on an agentic coding benchmark, surpassing Sonnet 4.6's 58.1% and nearing Opus 4.8's 69.2%.

While Opus 4.8 remains the preferred choice for tasks demanding the highest accuracy and complex judgment calls, Sonnet 5 provides a more cost-effective alternative for developers. Anthropic suggests users can balance cost and performance by choosing between Sonnet 5 and Opus 4.8 based on their specific needs.

Testers have reported that Sonnet 5 successfully completes complex, multi-part tasks that previously caused earlier versions to stall. Its ability to autonomously check its own output and execute end-to-end jobs, such as updating account tiers and sending announcements, makes it a valuable tool for automation.

On the safety front, Sonnet 5 exhibits a reduced rate of undesirable behaviors, including cooperation with misuse and deception, compared to its predecessor. It is more adept at refusing malicious requests and resisting prompt injection attacks, while also hallucinating and engaging in sycophantic behavior less frequently.

However, Sonnet 5's capabilities in performing dangerous cybersecurity tasks are noted to be lower than Anthropic's current Opus models. Despite this, the model is praised for its consistent and clean refusal of unsafe requests, a crucial feature for applications handling sensitive operations.

headline_marked: Acti [[puts AI agents in smartphone keyboards]] for iOS and Android
headline: Acti puts AI agents in smartphone keyboards for iOS and Android
summary: Acti's new keyboard brings AI tools directly into apps like email, messaging, and social media.
details: Acti, a Singapore-based startup, has launched an agentic keyboard for iOS and Android that brings AI tools directly into the apps users already use. The keyboard, powered by Google's Gemini models, can take actions on behalf of the user, such as suggesting local recommendations or sharing live stock prices.

The keyboard features a 'Skills' system, which allows users to program custom shortcuts to trigger multi-step tasks automatically. For example, users can translate a message or instantly share a meeting link with a single key press.

Acti's business model plans to generate revenue via subscriptions that offer users more advanced AI models, higher daily usage limits, and other premium features. The company has just closed on $5.3 million in seed funding, led by BITKRAFT Ventures.
The app prioritizes user privacy, with a local-first model that keeps personal context on the device by default. Users can also create and share custom 'Skills' publicly through a Skills marketplace.
